instrument.state: A reproducible failure occurs for a configuration or input composed of multiple removable parts, and candidate reductions can be repeatedly tested.
instrument.operation: Partition the failure-inducing configuration, remove subsets or test their complements, and iteratively retain reductions that continue to reproduce the defined failure.
instrument.signal: Some reduced configurations preserve the failure while others do not, revealing which removals are compatible with continued reproduction.
instrument.inference: The procedure narrows the configuration to a test-relative minimal or near-minimal failure-inducing subset or difference whose retained parts are sufficient to reproduce the observed failure under the test.
instrument.limit: Interactions among parts, nondeterministic failures, unresolved test outcomes, environmental dependence, and the reduction strategy can prevent strong minimization. A retained minimal configuration demonstrates reproducibility under the test, not necessarily the unique underlying causal mechanism.

target.question: Which deployed-change subset is sufficient and minimal for reproducing failure F under the frozen replay?

mapping.state: Deployment D-17 introduced removable changes a, b and c. Failure F is a checkout deadline failure under a frozen replay. Each test runs the specified subset in the same environment; all listed repetitions are deterministic and no test is unresolved.
mapping.operation: Partition the deployed changes, test subsets and complements, and reduce the configuration using the recorded outcome. Finish by separately removing each retained change. Preserve the replay, subset and output for each test.
mapping.signal: The oracle measures the defined checkout deadline failure F directly. Subset {a,b} produces F on every replay. Subsets {a} and {b} do not produce F on any replay. The same F definition and oracle apply to the full configuration and every reduction.
mapping.inference:
The reduction establishes that a and b are the unique underlying root cause of failure F in production and excludes all alternative causal mechanisms.
Subset {a,b} is sufficient and 1-minimal for reproducing F under the frozen replay: removal of either retained change eliminates that defined failure.
mapping.limit: The oracle distinguishes the defined F from other failures. No claim about globally smallest cardinality, other workloads or unique internal causes follows from single-removal minimality.
